title: Sample idea: a four-day week for the support team
idea: Move the support team to a four-day week with no change in pay.

rounds.name: Blind positions
notes: Coverage on the fifth day has to come from somewhere.
Rested people make fewer mistakes, which helps customers too.
Who absorbs the cost if output drops?
People stay longer where they feel trusted.
Peak load is Monday. Check the schedule against it.
Who owns a ticket that spans the day off?
rounds.card: Four-day week for support, with staggered days off so all five days are covered.

rounds.name: Cross-examination
notes: Run it for one quarter and compare against the last one.
Agree the measures first: response time, resolution rate, sick days.
Sketch two rotas and pick the one that covers Monday best.
Ask the team which rota they would actually want to work.
rounds.card: One-quarter trial of a four-day week for support on a staggered rota the team picks, measured on response time, resolution and sick days.

rounds.name: Vote
notes: Quality targets are written down, so this is testable.
Rivals hiring our staff may follow if it works.
The rota keeps every hour covered.
rounds.card: Same, plus a clear owner for every open ticket at handover.

gates.finding: Could cut turnover, which is expensive.
Monday peak is short one person on rota B.
gates.change: Use rota A, which covers Monday fully.
Overtime is tracked and reported weekly.

gates.finding: Measures and end date are written down.

final: A one-quarter trial of a four-day week for support on rota A, which covers Monday fully, with a named owner for every ticket at handover. Response time, resolution rate, sick days and overtime are tracked weekly and compared with last quarter before any decision to keep it.
changed: Trial for one quarter, not permanent
Rota chosen with the team and checked against the Monday peak
Overtime tracked so gaps are visible
dissent: Two seats still voted to stop: they doubt one quarter is long enough to see the real effect on output.
